lc_person: Thomas Wilke, born 1975, media and communication scholar; professor of cultural education at PH Ludwigsburg since 2017; author of work on DDR television and discotheques.
item_person: Thomas Wilke, born 1964, biologist and professor of systematics and biodiversity at Justus Liebig University Giessen.

evidence.says: LC heading is Wilke, Thomas, 1975-. Its source note for Fiktionale Geschichtssendungen im DDR-Fernsehen (2007), p. 242, reports birth in 1975. It also cites Schallplattenunterhalter und Diskothek in der DDR (2009), a media and communication dissertation at Martin-Luther-Universität, and a publisher biography identifying the PH Ludwigsburg professor since 2017. External links nevertheless include the biologist’s GND 1093438371 and Q2428157.

Institutional CV identifies Thomas Wilke as professor of cultural education since 2017, previously at Tübingen, with a 2008 Halle-Wittenberg doctorate on DJs and discotheques in the DDR; this matches LC’s source notes.
GND record for the media and communication scholar gives birth year 1975, identifies the Tübingen and PH Ludwigsburg appointments, and explicitly links to Wikidata Q95330369.

Separate GND record identifies a biologist at Justus Liebig University Giessen and lists the 2001 zoology habilitation Cryptic radiations in the superfamily Rissooidea. It explicitly links to Q2428157 and the German Wikipedia biography of the biologist, while also carrying the conflicting LC identifier.
Biography identifies Thomas Wilke as a biologist born in 1964 and professor of zoology and biodiversity at Giessen; its Wikidata link targets Q2428157.

Institutional CV confirms the biologist’s distinct career: biology diploma in 1989, zoology doctorate in 1994, habilitation in 2001, and professor and head of the Systematics and Biodiversity Group at Giessen since 2004.

notes: Different people, rather than a birth-year typo. The supplied key_evidence is empty, so the graph person cannot be independently matched beyond the shared name. LC and the biologist’s authority cluster contain conflicting cross-links. Direct Wikidata page and entity-data requests failed; QID identification uses explicit GND and Wikipedia links. The replacement QID is supported by the media scholar’s GND record.
